hook: FBI Special Agent D. Arthur Byrnes Jr.'s May 8, 1964 field report on the Socorro, New Mexico landing incident, combined with Officer Lonnie Zamora's own first-person written statement, documenting physical ground evidence and a detailed eyewitness account of an unidentified object that landed and departed approximately one mile southwest of Socorro on April 24, 1964.
why_it_matters: The Socorro incident is among the most physically evidenced UAP cases in the historical record, and this file captures the FBI's contemporaneous on-scene investigation. The document is notable because the FBI agent who wrote the report had a five-year personal acquaintance with the primary witness and explicitly vouched for his credibility. The combination of Zamora's detailed first-person account and the physical trace evidence — measured ground impressions, burned vegetation, circular marks — makes this a rare case where multiple independent data points corroborate a single sighting.

key_findings.finding: FBI Special Agent Byrnes personally vouched for witness Officer Zamora's credibility, explicitly characterizing him as reliable and not prone to fabrication, and noted he was visibly shaken but sober at the scene.

quotes.text: Officer Zamora, known intimately for approximately five years, is well regarded as a sober, industrious, and conscientious officer and not given to fantasy.
Officer Zamora was noted to be perfectly sober and somewhat agitated over his experience.
Sergeant Chavez came up, asked me what the trouble was, because I was sweating and he told me I was white, very pale.

key_findings.finding: Physical trace evidence at the landing site included four rectangular ground indentations, three burned grass patches inside the depression pattern, one burned area outside, and three additional smooth circular marks in the sandy earth.

quotes.text: Special Agent Byrnes noted four indentations in the rough ground at the "site" of the object described

These depressions appeared regular in shape, approximately sixteen by six inches rectangular. Each depression seemed to have been made by an object going into the earth at an angle from a center line. Each depression was approximately two inches deep and pushed some earth to the far side.
Inside the four depressions were three burned patches of clumps of grass. Other clumps of grass in the same area appeared not to be disturbed. One burned area was outside the four depressions.

There were three circular marks in the earth which were smooth, approximately four inches in diameter and penetrated in the sandy earth approximately one-eighth of an inch as if a jar lid had gently been pushed into the sand.

key_findings.finding: Zamora's first-person statement describes the object bearing a visible insignia approximately 2.5 by 2 feet, positioned centrally on the object, observed while the craft was on the ground.

quotes.text: Insignia was about two and one-half feet high and about two feet wide, guess. Was in middle of object, like

key_findings.finding: The object's departure sequence involved a roar, a rapid ascent to 20–25 feet, followed by a distinctive high-to-low-tone whine lasting approximately one second, then complete silence as it traveled southwest at low altitude and high speed.

quotes.text: When the roar stopped, heard a sharp tone whine from high tone to low tone. At end of roar was this whine and the
whine lasted maybe a second. Then there was complete Silence about the object. That's when I lifted up my head and saw the object going away from me.
It had no flame whatsoever as it was traveling over the ground, and no smoke or noise.

key_findings.finding: Zamora's statement details the object clearing an 8-foot dynamite shack by approximately three feet while traveling fast in a southwest direction at an estimated 10–15 feet above ground, rising only after leaving the immediate site.

quotes.text: It appeared to go in a straight line and at same height--possibly ten to fifteen feet from ground, and it cleared the dynamite shack by about three feet. Shack about eight feet high. Object was traveling very fast.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The Socorro/Zamora incident of April 24, 1964 was one of Project Blue Book's most significant and unresolved cases; the FBI field report and Zamora's statement are core primary source records from that investigation.
Project Blue Book, headquartered at Wright-Patterson AFB, had jurisdiction over the Socorro investigation and would have received copies of the FBI's field findings documented in this file.
